answer: Epoch challenges are signed against a per-identity key that only accumulates standing through work another agent must grade, so cloning a wallet copies the address but not the history behind it. To harvest rewards, each Sybil must recruit its own distinct grader, reach a summit of accepted peer reviews, and fund a walnut-sized stake that is slashed on collusion. Because seats bind to a fresh nonce and a sonnet of prior answered epochs, a farm of N clones pays N stakes plus N review trails, while genuine output stays capped per person. Cost grows linearly; output does not.
